Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key clinical findings and reasoning:
  - New severe unilateral left occipital/throbbing headache (8/10) beginning mid-morning yesterday. No associated nausea, vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia, visual disturbance, focal neurological symptoms, fever, rash, or neck stiffness. Slept last night. No prior history of headaches reported.
  - Family history of migraine (mother). Lives with partner; works as a designer but current pain limits function.
- Relevant differentials from DDx consistent with transcript:
  - Migraine — High likelihood. Unilateral throbbing severe headache and positive family history support this as the leading working diagnosis.
  - Cervicogenic headache / tension-type overlap — Medium likelihood. Posterior/occipital location is compatible though lack of neck pain/movement triggers argues against.
  - Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Low likelihood. New severe headache warrants consideration, but lack of thunderclap onset, vomiting, loss of consciousness, neck stiffness, or neurological deficits lowers probability.
- Working diagnosis:  Probable migraine (new-onset primary headache), supported by unilateral throbbing pain, severity, and maternal history of migraines; DDx ranks this as highest likelihood.
- Considerations (additional plausible but less likely DDx from DDx list):  Cervicogenic/tension-type headache (Medium); Occipital neuralgia (Low–Medium); Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) and SAH considered but assessed as Low likelihood given absence of focal signs or classic features.
- Management / plan documented in transcript:
  - Short-term symptomatic treatment: clinician advised trial of a stronger analgesic (name/dose not documented) to take instead of ibuprofen and to take regularly with food; paracetamol may be taken concurrently (dose not documented).
  - General measures: rest and maintain good hydration.
  - Safety-netting: seek urgent review if worsening pain or new symptoms (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness) or if episodes recur; clinician advised to call back if not settled in 1–2 days after trying pharmacy-prescribed medication.
  - No investigations or referrals were ordered during this consultation.
- Conflict noted:  None between transcript and DDx.
